title: Awarapan 2 Trailer Drops With Emraan Hashmi Returning as Shivam After 19 Years
excerpt: The official trailer for the Vishesh Films sequel arrived on August 6, showing a darker, revenge-driven storyline starring Hashmi alongside Disha Patani and Shabana Azmi ahead of the August 14 theatrical release.
body:
• The Awarapan 2 trailer released on August 6 reveals Emraan Hashmi reprising the role of Shivam from the 2007 original in a revenge-driven narrative
  • The film stars Hashmi alongside Disha Patani and Shabana Azmi, is directed by Nitin Kakkar, and produced by Vishesh Bhatt under Vishesh Films
  • The CBFC cleared the film on August 5 with a U/A 16+ certificate and a 140-minute runtime after ordering four minutes of cuts to violent and drug-related scenes
  • Awarapan 2 releases theatrically on August 14, Independence Day, clashing with Sunny Deol's Batwara 1947

Vishesh Films dropped the official trailer for Awarapan 2 on Wednesday, giving audiences their first extended look at Emraan Hashmi's return to the role that helped define his early career. The trailer positions the sequel as a darker, more intense entry in Bollywood's crime-romance genre, with Hashmi's Shivam returning 19 years after the original to settle unfinished scores.

"Is baar yeh awarapan khatam hoga, ya main" — this time the vagrancy ends, or I do — serves as the film's tagline, signaling a narrative driven by vengeance and closure rather than the wandering romance of the 2007 original.

What the Trailer Reveals

The two-and-a-half minute trailer opens on a haunted Shivam, described as "a man haunted by grief and loss, searching for a purpose for his life." The footage mixes intense action sequences with emotional confrontations, featuring Hashmi in what appears to be his most physically demanding role in years.

Disha Patani plays the female lead opposite Hashmi, while veteran actress Shabana Azmi takes on a pivotal role that the trailer suggests may carry significant dramatic weight. The film is directed by Nitin Kakkar and written by Sanjay Masoom and Bilal Siddiqui, with music composed by Jeet Ganguly, Amaal Mallik, and Mithoon.

CBFC Clearance and Release Strategy

The trailer drop comes one day after the Central Board of Film Certification cleared Awarapan 2 with a U/A 16+ certificate on August 5. The CBFC ordered four minutes of deletions and 20 seconds of replacements, targeting scenes depicting extreme violence, child trafficking, and drug consumption. The certified runtime is 140 minutes and 20 seconds.

The film releases theatrically on August 14, coinciding with Independence Day — traditionally one of Bollywood's most lucrative release windows. It will clash directly with Sunny Deol's Batwara 1947, another patriotic-themed release.

"It's our fortune and luck that we get to share this release date with Sunny Deol."

— Vishesh Bhatt, Producer, Awarapan 2

The Sequel's Journey

Awarapan 2 has had a protracted path to release. Originally scheduled for April 2026, the film was pushed to Independence Day in a strategic repositioning. The soundtrack — featuring tracks "Ve Junoon," "Yeh Awarapan," "Tera Mera Rishta," and a revived "Toh Phir Aao" — has already generated attention, including a controversy over what music director Amaal Mallik called "paid PR" attacks on the album. The official teaser, released June 29, trended at number one on YouTube's movies chart.

The film is produced on an estimated budget of ₹25–30 crore, with theatrical distribution handled by Pen Marudhar.

What's Next

With just eight days between the trailer drop and theatrical release, Vishesh Films is banking on a compressed marketing sprint. The Independence Day box office will test whether Emraan Hashmi's star power and the Awarapan brand can compete against Sunny Deol's established holiday-release track record. Early buzz from the teaser suggests strong audience curiosity, but the U/A 16+ rating — rather than the adult certificate many expected — could widen its potential audience.
